posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Lam Research and ASE expansions; data center shifts; CPO system architecture initiative; 2D-transistor interface solution; USENIX HW security; patent suits; image sensors; programmable AI memtransistor; Nvidia's new plan; earnings; Tier IV's L4 auto chip.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: ASE subsidiary SPIL is investing $3.1 billion in a new Taiwan-based facility to expand CoWoS capacity for AI chips, with production slated to begin in 2028.
Data center architecture is undergoing a major shift toward 1-megawatt racks, necessitating fundamental changes in power delivery, cooling systems, and 3D-IC packaging to support AI workloads.

Rhodium Group projects that China's legacy-chip capacity will approach 50% of global output by 2030, as domestic equipment manufacturers continue to scale despite restrictions on leading-edge AI hardware.
Lam Research announced a $3 billion, five-year investment to expand its global R&D lab network, aiming to increase its experimental capacity by over 50%.
Sony and TSMC have finalized a joint venture in Japan for next-generation image sensors, with Sony contributing approximately $2.9 billion to lead the project.

posts.title: 2026.33: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of August 10, 2026, including the capital constraint, AI writing, and a tale of two cities.
bullets: Nvidia is implementing new financial engineering mechanisms to secure long-duration capital, signaling a shift in how AI infrastructure is funded as the industry faces potential capital constraints.
The reliance on creative financing and equity taps by major players like Google suggests that AI investment is not yet self-sustaining, raising concerns about the sustainability of current margins.

New EU regulations mandating the labeling of AI-generated content are being met with industry resistance, as critics argue such mandates fail to account for the evolving nature of human-AI collaboration.

The divergence between New York City's resilient financial sector and Hollywood's declining local production base highlights how network effects can protect some industries while leaving others vulnerable to geographic outsourcing.

posts.title: Li Auto's chip ambitions extend from assisted driving to data centers, report says
posts.summary:
Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto is in the early stages of developing an in-house cloud inference chip to handle workloads currently managed by GPUs.
The project aims to leverage the dataflow architecture used in the company's vehicle-side assisted driving chips to reduce R&D costs through shared design and software tools.
While technically feasible, the company faces significant challenges in achieving cost-competitive inference performance compared to established cloud-scale solutions.
The initiative reflects a broader trend of automotive companies seeking vertical integration in AI hardware to optimize both vehicle performance and backend data processing.

posts.title: Li Auto's L6 tops 400,000 cumulative deliveries as revamped model revives demand
posts.summary:
The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto's L6 SUV has surpassed 400,000 cumulative deliveries in less than 27 months, cementing its status as a core volume driver for the company.
Demand for the model has rebounded sharply following the July 2026 launch of a revamped version, with deliveries reaching approximately 9,000 units in the first half of August.
The new L6 features significant technical upgrades, including a 51 kWh battery for extended range and the integration of Li Auto's in-house Mach M100 assisted driving chip.
The successful refresh of the L6 is a critical component of Li Auto's broader strategy to modernize its L-series lineup and recover from a temporary sales slump earlier this year.

posts.title: Geely Farizon's first overseas plant starts operations in Indonesia
posts.summary:
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Farizon has commenced operations at its first overseas knock-down (KD) assembly plant in Indonesia, located southeast of Jakarta.
The facility began production with the V8E all-electric logistics vehicle, which has been specifically calibrated for local road conditions and tropical climates.
This localized production strategy is designed to bypass import tariffs, streamline supply chains, and lower operating costs in the competitive Southeast Asian market.
The company plans to gradually expand its localized product lineup and integrate further into the Indonesian industrial chain to support long-term growth.
